text:
mike: quick follow-up to the span-slimming RFC — i wanted to surface a few edge cases we missed when mapping spans -> cost buckets. thinking out loud before i write a formal patch.
jamie: go for it — which cases are you worried about?
sarah: curious too. is this about losing billing keys when we drop attributes from leaf spans?
mike: exactly. if we aggressively prune span tags for compactness we might lose the tenant/billing context if it only lives on a deep DB span. that would break attribution for some tail queries.
ajax: i mean, we debated having a small "joinpoint envelope" on the root that carries: billing_key, service_tier, sample_cohort. keep that across the trace, even if child spans are trimmed.
jamie: i like the envelope idea. lightweight and explicit. downside: requires SDKs/agents to write the joinpoint early.
alex: another option: keep a tiny marker on any span that originates external network requests (eg http/db), with a hashed billing_key reference. ingest can deref the hash to the full key during enrich.
mike: hashing helps privacy and size, but adds lookup complexity. if lookups fail (cache miss) we need a graceful fallback or we lose attribution.
infra-bot: deploy: rollout canary started for obsv-agent v0.20 -> 5% of edge infra at 2025-06-12T09:00Z :rocket:
carmen: pragmatic compromise: 1) require joinpoint envelope on root for new SDKs 2) accept hashed ref on older agents and add a best-effort late-enrich lookup in ingest 3) treat missing lookups as "unattributed" but surface as telemetry so we can measure impact.
sarah: +1. we should also add a migration flag in the ingest manifest so queries can join on either billing_key or hashed_ref for a window.
jamie: good call. what's the expected lift on the ingest side for late-enrich? i can scope if we decide.
alex: estimate: small index + cache (redis) and a bloom filter to reduce misses. probably 2-3 engineer-weeks for a minimal path (cache + fallback queue).
mike: ok, action items: jamie to write an enrichment shim RFC that details the joinpoint envelope shape and fallbacks; alex to sketch cache+lookup perf numbers; carmen to draft rollout policy + canary gating.
carmen: will do. also want a dashboard: % of traces with joinpoint present vs hashed_only vs missing. that will be our migration signal.
sarah: should we add a short schema snippet here? example joinpoint envelope:

```
joinpoint: {
  billing_key: "acct:acme-123",
  billing_key_hash: "h1:9f3a...",
  sample_cohort: "cohort-v2",
  sdk_version: "obsv-js@0.20"
}
```

(note: we'll store the full billing_key only in controlled envelopes; hashes used where size matters)
mike: perfect. can we avoid embedding full keys in leaf spans? keep full key on root only and hashes elsewhere.
jamie: yep — edge agents should stamp root + hashed refs. ingest will materialize billing_key when possible.
infra-bot: note: tracing-telemetry pipeline has a quota for late-lookups (100k/day) configured in canary. monitor please.
alex: i'll post perf tests by EOD next Tuesday.
mike: thanks all — i'll sync this into the follow-up RFC draft and tag you for review. :thumbsup:
